This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Elevated Token:		Yes



Impersonation Level:		Impersonation



New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		SYSTEM

	Account Domain:		NT AUTHORITY

	Logon ID:		0x3E7

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x304

	Process Name:		C:\Windows\System32\services.exe



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	-

	Source Port:		-



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Advapi  

	Authentication Package:	Negotiate

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{755b29ee-d3bd-37fb-8a03-132418dc659b}



Process Information:

	Source Network Address:	fe80::ef0e:4bda:289b:a308

	Source Port:		63931

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		WIN-70C1LAV3I79$

	Account Domain:		LAB.LOCAL

	Logon ID:		0x37DD206

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{f6a4dc14-a783-5d30-2daf-1a94f6310b3a}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x0

	Process Name:		-



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	::1

	Source Port:		51201



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Process ID:		0x304

	Process Name:		C:\Windows\System32\services.exe

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	-

	Source Port:		-

	Logon Process:		Advapi  

	Authentication Package:	Negotiate

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Logon Type:		5

	Restricted Admin Mode:	-

	Remote Credential Guard:	-

	Virtual Account:		No

	Elevated Token:		Yes



Impersonation Level:		Impersonation



New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		SYSTEM

	Account Domain:		NT AUTHORITY

	Logon ID:		0x3E7

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x304

	Process Name:		C:\Windows\System32\services.exe



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	-

	Source Port:		-



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Advapi  

	Authentication Package:	Negotiate

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).

The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Source Port:		54347

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.

The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).

The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Source Port:		0

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

Message=An account was successfully logged on.



Subject:

	Security ID:		S-1-0-0

	Account Name:		-

	Account Domain:		-

	Logon ID:		0x0



Logon Information:

	Logon Type:		3

	Restricted Admin Mode:	-

	Remote Credential Guard:	-

	Virtual Account:		No

	Elevated Token:		Yes



Impersonation Level:		Impersonation



New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		WIN-70C1LAV3I79$

	Account Domain:		LAB.LOCAL

	Logon ID:		0x340105B

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{3627e909-b352-60f2-2474-ca1a87eaaa6a}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x0

	Process Name:		-



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	fe80::ef0e:4bda:289b:a308

	Source Port:		62179



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

Logon Information:

	Logon Type:		3

	Remote Credential Guard:	-

	Virtual Account:		No

	Elevated Token:		Yes



Impersonation Level:		Impersonation



New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		WIN-70C1LAV3I79$

	Account Domain:		LAB.LOCAL

	Logon ID:		0x339A79B

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{f6a4dc14-a783-5d30-2daf-1a94f6310b3a}

	Process ID:		0x0

	Process Name:		-



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	::1

	Source Port:		62121



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		WIN-70C1LAV3I79$

	Account Domain:		LAB.LOCAL

	Logon ID:		0x337B13E

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{f6a4dc14-a783-5d30-2daf-1a94f6310b3a}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x0

	Process Name:		-



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	::1

	Source Port:		62092



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

	Logon ID:		0x3333E5C

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{755b29ee-d3bd-37fb-8a03-132418dc659b}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x0

	Process Name:		-



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	::1

	Source Port:		0



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Kerberos

	Authentication Package:	Kerberos

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

Subject:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		WIN-70C1LAV3I79$

	Account Domain:		LAB

	Logon ID:		0x3E7



Logon Information:

	Logon Type:		5

	Restricted Admin Mode:	-

	Remote Credential Guard:	-

	Virtual Account:		No

	Elevated Token:		Yes



Impersonation Level:		Impersonation



New Logon:

	Security ID:		S-1-5-18

	Account Name:		SYSTEM

	Account Domain:		NT AUTHORITY

	Logon ID:		0x3E7

	Linked Logon ID:		0x0

	Network Account Name:	-

	Network Account Domain:	-

	Logon GUID:		{00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000}



Process Information:

	Process ID:		0x304

	Process Name:		C:\Windows\System32\services.exe



Network Information:

	Workstation Name:	-

	Source Network Address:	-

	Source Port:		-



Detailed Authentication Information:

	Logon Process:		Advapi  

	Authentication Package:	Negotiate

	Transited Services:	-

	Package Name (NTLM only):	-

	Key Length:		0



This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.

This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.



The subject fields indicate the account on the local system which requested the logon. This is most commonly a service such as the Server service, or a local process such as Winlogon.exe or Services.exe.



The logon type field indicates the kind of logon that occurred. The most common types are 2 (interactive) and 3 (network).



The New Logon fields indicate the account for whom the new logon was created, i.e. the account that was logged on.



The network fields indicate where a remote logon request originated. Workstation name is not always available and may be left blank in some cases.



The impersonation level field indicates the extent to which a process in the logon session can impersonate.



The authentication information fields provide detailed information about this specific logon request.

	- Logon GUID is a unique identifier that can be used to correlate this event with a KDC event.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.

	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.

	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested.
